name: Google Calendar
description: Find, create, update and delete events in Google Calendar, and check when people are free.

timeOf.description: A Google start/end object: `date` for all-day events, `dateTime` (with an optional zone) otherwise.
timeOf.body: value == undefined ? undefined : (allDay ? {date: substring(value, 0, 10)} : compactObject({dateTime: value, timeZone}))

eventOf.description: A Google Calendar event, flattened: one ISO start/end, attendees with plain names.
eventOf.body:
{
                id: e.id,
                status: e.status,
                summary: e.summary,
                description: e.description,
                location: e.location,
                start: e.start.dateTime ?? e.start.date,
                end: e.end.dateTime ?? e.end.date,
                allDay: e.start.date != undefined,
                timeZone: e.start.timeZone,
                organizer: e.organizer.email,
                attendees: map(default(e.attendees, []), a => compactObject({email: a.email, name: a.displayName, response: a.responseStatus, organizer: a.organizer})),
                meetLink: e.hangoutLink,
                htmlLink: e.htmlLink,
                recurringEventId: e.recurringEventId,
                created: e.created,
                updated: e.updated
            } | compactObject

auth.label: Sign in with Google
auth.setup:
1. In the Google Cloud console, create (or pick) a project and **enable the Google Calendar API**.
2. Configure the **OAuth consent screen** and add the scopes `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`.
3. Create an **OAuth client ID** of type *Web application*. Add your Conduit callback URL (for example `https://app.example/conduit/auth/callback`) as an **authorized redirect URI**.
4. Give the client id and secret to Conduit: `createConduit({ clients: { 'google-calendar': { id, secret } } })`.
